question: Which of the following is/are controlled by the use of insecticides in crop protection management?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Insects.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Insecticides are chemical substances specifically formulated to kill or control insects that damage crops, such as aphids, borers and locusts. (कीटनाशक — कीड़ों को नियंत्रित करने वाले रसायन)

 

• Different pests need different chemicals: herbicides control weeds, fungicides control fungal diseases, and rodenticides control rodents. Using the wrong class of pesticide will not control the intended pest.

 

• Excessive or careless use of insecticides can kill useful insects (like bees and predators of pests), pollute soil and water, and leave harmful residues on food crops — this is why Integrated Pest Management (IPM) is now encouraged.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pesticide is the umbrella term for all chemicals used to kill pests, of which insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and rodenticides are sub-categories.

 

• Common insecticide groups include organochlorines (e.g. DDT), organophosphates and pyrethroids.

 

• Biological/organic pest control (using natural predators, neem-based products) is promoted as an eco-friendlier alternative to chemical insecticides.

 

NOTE

 

• Virus (Option A): Plant viral diseases are usually controlled indirectly, by controlling the insect vectors (like aphids) that spread them, not by insecticides directly killing the virus.

 

• Weeds (Option B): Controlled using herbicides (weedicides), not insecticides.

 

• Fungus (Option D): Controlled using fungicides, a separate class of crop-protection chemical.

question: A triangular glass prism has how many rectangular lateral surfaces?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Three.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A triangular prism has 2 triangular bases (the two ends) and 3 rectangular lateral (side) faces joining them. (त्रिभुजाकार प्रिज्म — 3 आयताकार पार्श्व फलक)

 

• In optics, light entering through one rectangular face and leaving through another (inclined) rectangular face is what causes a glass prism to disperse white light into its constituent colours (VIBGYOR).

 

• In general, a prism with an n-sided polygonal base has n rectangular lateral faces and 2 polygonal bases, giving a total of (n+2) faces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The angle of the prism is the angle between its two refracting (slanting) surfaces; for a standard triangular prism it is often 60°.

 

• Dispersion of light through a prism happens because different colours (wavelengths) bend by different amounts — violet bends the most and red the least, since violet has the shortest wavelength.

 

• Newton's classic prism experiment, and Newton's disc (which recombines VIBGYOR into white light), are commonly tested alongside this topic.

 

NOTE

 

• Four (Option A): Would apply to a prism with a quadrilateral (4-sided) base, not a triangular one.

 

• Two (Option C): This is the number of triangular (end/base) faces of the prism, not the lateral faces.

 

• One (Option D): Not correct for any standard prism shape used in optics.

question: Which of the following organisms multiplies by the means of multiple fission mode of reproduction?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Plasmodium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plasmodium, the parasite that causes malaria, reproduces asexually inside the human red blood cells by multiple fission (schizogony) — a single nucleus divides repeatedly before the cytoplasm divides, producing many daughter cells (merozoites) at once. (बहु-विखंडन — प्लाज्मोडियम)

 

• In multiple fission, the parent cell's nucleus divides into many nuclei first; the cell membrane then encloses each nucleus separately, so many daughter organisms form simultaneously from one parent, unlike binary fission where only two form.

 

• Malaria spreads to humans through the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito, which acts as the vector.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fission in unicellular organisms is of two main types: binary fission (one cell divides into two, e.g. Amoeba, Paramecium, bacteria) and multiple fission (one cell divides into many, e.g. Plasmodium).

 

• Leishmania, the parasite causing kala-azar (visceral leishmaniasis), reproduces mainly by binary fission.

 

• Other asexual modes seen in simple organisms include budding (Hydra, yeast) and fragmentation (Spirogyra).

 

NOTE

 

• Leishmania (Option A): Reproduces by binary fission, not multiple fission.

 

• Garden pea (Option B): A flowering plant that reproduces sexually; famous as the subject of Mendel's genetics experiments.

 

• Hibiscus (Option C): A flowering plant reproducing sexually (and also propagated by cuttings), not by fission.

question: Which of the following is a general physical property of nonmetals?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dull appearance (non-lustrous).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nonmetals generally have a dull (non-lustrous) appearance, unlike metals which are shiny/lustrous. (अधातु — चमकरहित सतह)

 

• Nonmetals are typically poor conductors of heat and electricity (graphite being a notable exception), are brittle when solid (not malleable or ductile), and often have comparatively lower melting and boiling points than metals.

 

• Common physical properties of nonmetals: not sonorous, low density, and they can exist as solids, liquids (bromine) or gases (oxygen, nitrogen) at room temperature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Metals are typically lustrous, malleable, ductile, sonorous, good conductors of heat/electricity, and have high melting/boiling points (mercury being a liquid-metal exception).

 

• Metalloids (like silicon, germanium, arsenic) show intermediate properties of both metals and nonmetals and are often used as semiconductors.

 

• Nonmetals form acidic or neutral oxides, while metals generally form basic oxides.

 

NOTE

 

• High electrical conductivity (Option A): A property of metals, not nonmetals (graphite is the exception among nonmetals).

 

• Malleability and ductility (Option B): Metals can be hammered into sheets (malleable) and drawn into wires (ductile); nonmetals are brittle and break instead.

 

• High melting and boiling points (Option D): Generally true of metals; most nonmetals have comparatively lower melting/boiling points.

question: For the life processes, the transfer of a source of energy from outside the body of the organism is called ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is nutrition.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Nutrition is the life process by which an organism takes in food (a source of energy and raw material) from outside its body and utilises it for growth, repair and energy. (पोषण — बाहर से ऊर्जा स्रोत ग्रहण करना)

 

• Nutrition is broadly of two types: autotrophic (organisms like green plants make their own food via photosynthesis) and heterotrophic (organisms like animals and fungi depend on other organisms for food).

 

• Nutrition is distinct from digestion — digestion is only the breakdown of the food already taken in, while nutrition covers the whole process of obtaining and using that food/energy source.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• The seven basic life processes commonly listed are: nutrition, respiration, transportation, excretion, control and coordination, growth, and reproduction.

 

• Respiration is the process of breaking down food to release energy within the cell (using oxygen in aerobic respiration), which is different from simply acquiring food.

 

• Excretion is the removal of nitrogenous metabolic waste products from the body.

 

NOTE

 

• Respiration (Option A): Releases energy stored in food inside the body; it does not describe taking in the energy source from outside.

 

• Digestion (Option C): The mechanical and chemical breakdown of ingested food into simpler, absorbable molecules — a sub-step within nutrition.

 

• Excretion (Option D): Removal of waste products from the body, unrelated to intake of an energy source.

question: Electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed paths called:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shells or orbitals.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to the Bohr–Bury atomic model, electrons revolve around the nucleus in fixed, defined circular paths called shells (or orbits/energy levels), denoted K, L, M, N... (from the nucleus outward). (कोश/कक्षा — इलेक्ट्रॉन के निश्चित पथ)

 

• Each shell can hold a maximum number of electrons given by the formula 2n², where n is the shell number (K=2, L=8, M=18, N=32).

 

• Electrons revolving in these fixed shells do not radiate energy, which is why atoms are normally stable — energy is absorbed or emitted only when an electron jumps between shells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nucleons is the collective term for protons and neutrons present in the nucleus, not the electron's path.

 

• The valence shell is the outermost shell of an atom, and the electrons in it (valence electrons) determine the chemical properties of the element.

 

• Quarks are elementary particles that make up protons and neutrons; they are unrelated to electron paths.

 

NOTE

 

• Nucleons (Option A): Protons + neutrons inside the nucleus — not the electron orbit.

 

• Elliptical paths (Option B): Bohr's model of a simple atom uses circular paths; elliptical orbits were a refinement suggested later by Sommerfeld, not the basic term asked here.

 

• Quarks (Option D): Sub-particles of protons/neutrons, unrelated to the concept of electron shells.

question: Neurons have many short, branched parts or processes attached to cell body called ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is dendrites.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dendrites are the short, thin, highly-branched processes that extend from the cell body (cyton) of a neuron and receive nerve impulses from other neurons, carrying them towards the cell body. (द्रुमिका/डेंड्राइट — तंत्रिका कोशिका का शाखित भाग)

 

• A typical neuron has three main parts: the cell body (with nucleus), many dendrites (input), and one long axon (output), which carries the impulse away from the cell body to the next neuron or effector organ.

 

• The junction where one neuron's axon meets another neuron's dendrite is called a synapse, across which the impulse is transmitted chemically (via neurotransmitters).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The nerve impulse in a neuron always travels in one direction: dendrite → cell body → axon → synapse.

 

• The axon is usually a single, long fibre (sometimes covered by a fatty myelin sheath that speeds up conduction) that carries the impulse away from the cell body.

 

• Neurons are classified as sensory, motor and relay (association) neurons based on their function.

 

NOTE

 

• Axons (Option B): The single long fibre that carries impulses AWAY from the cell body, not the many short branched receiving processes.

 

• Nerve endings (Option C): General term for the terminal branches of an axon at a synapse, not the receiving structures near the cell body.

 

• Nuclei (Option D): The nucleus is located within the cell body of the neuron and controls cell activities; it is not a branched process.

question: Which of the following life processes is NOT essential to maintain the life of an individual organism?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reproduction.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reproduction is essential for the continuation of the species, but an individual organism can live its entire life span without reproducing — so it is not essential for the survival of that particular individual. (जनन — प्रजाति के लिए आवश्यक, व्यष्टि जीव के लिए नहीं)

 

• In contrast, nutrition, respiration and excretion must occur continuously in every living individual — an organism cannot survive even briefly without obtaining energy (nutrition), releasing energy from food (respiration) and removing toxic waste (excretion).

 

• This distinction — individual-level essential processes versus species-level essential processes — is a classic NCERT-based conceptual question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• The seven basic life processes are: nutrition, respiration, transportation, excretion, control & coordination, growth, and reproduction.

 

• Growth and movement/responsiveness (control and coordination) are also generally considered essential to maintain life, though growth can slow drastically in a mature adult.

 

• Organisms that cannot reproduce (e.g. due to injury or sterility) can still survive normally as individuals as long as their other life processes continue.

 

NOTE

 

• Nutrition (Option B): Essential — without taking in food/energy, an organism cannot survive.

 

• Excretion (Option C): Essential — toxic metabolic wastes must be removed continuously, or they would poison the body.

 

• Respiration (Option D): Essential — without releasing energy from food, no life activity (including all other life processes) can occur.

question: A baby pulls a toy car along the ground. If the force and displacement are in the same direction, the work done is:
option_2: equal to the speed of the car
option_3: equal to the product of force and displacement
solution_text:
The correct answer is equal to the product of force and displacement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Physics, work done, W = F × d × cosθ, where θ is the angle between the applied force and the displacement. (कार्य = बल × विस्थापन, जब दोनों समदिश हों)

 

• When the force and displacement act in the same direction, θ = 0°, so cos 0° = 1, and the formula simplifies to W = F × d — the plain product of force and displacement.

 

• This is called positive work, since force helps the object move in its direction of motion (e.g. the baby's pull helping the car move forward).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SI unit of work is the joule (J), where 1 joule = 1 newton × 1 metre.

 

• Work done is zero when either the force is zero, the displacement is zero, or the force acts perpendicular to the displacement (θ = 90°), as when carrying a bag while walking horizontally.

 

• Work done is negative when the force acts opposite to the direction of displacement (θ = 180°), e.g. friction acting against a moving object.

 

NOTE

 

• Equal to zero (Option A): Only true if force ⊥ displacement, or if either quantity is zero — not the case here.

 

• Equal to the speed of the car (Option B): Speed and work are entirely different physical quantities with different units; this option is dimensionally meaningless.

 

• Negative (Option D): Would apply only if force and displacement were in opposite directions, which contradicts the question.

question: Liquids have:
option_1: a definite shape and a fixed volume
option_2: no definite shape and no fixed volume
option_3: no definite shape but have a fixed volume
option_4: a definite shape and no fixed volume
solution_text:
The correct answer is no definite shape but have a fixed volume.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Liquids take the shape of whatever container they are poured into (no fixed shape), but the quantity (volume) of liquid stays the same regardless of the container's shape (fixed volume). (द्रव — निश्चित आयतन, अनिश्चित आकार)

 

• This behaviour occurs because the intermolecular forces in liquids are moderate — strong enough to keep the particles close together (giving fixed volume) but weak enough to let particles slide past one another (giving no fixed shape).

 

• Liquids are nearly incompressible, like solids, because their particles are already closely packed with very little empty space between them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Solids have both a fixed shape and a fixed volume, since their particles are tightly packed in a fixed arrangement with strong intermolecular forces.

 

• Gases have neither a fixed shape nor a fixed volume — they expand to completely fill any container, because intermolecular forces are very weak and particles move freely.

 

• The three common states of matter are grouped by rate of diffusion, compressibility and density in the order solid < liquid < gas for diffusion/compressibility, and generally gas < liquid < solid for density.

 

NOTE

 

• Option A (definite shape and fixed volume): Describes solids, not liquids.

 

• Option B (no definite shape and no fixed volume): Describes gases, not liquids.

 

• Option D (definite shape and no fixed volume): This combination does not correspond to any common state of matter.

question: What is corrosion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chemical change.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Corrosion is a chemical change in which a metal, on exposure to air, moisture or other substances in its environment, gets slowly eaten away/converted into its compounds (usually oxides, sulphides or carbonates). (संक्षारण — धातु का रासायनिक क्षय)

 

• A well-known example is the rusting of iron, in which iron reacts with oxygen and moisture in air to form hydrated iron(III) oxide (Fe₂O₃·xH₂O), commonly called rust.

 

• Being a chemical change, corrosion produces a new substance (the metal compound) with different properties from the original metal, and it is generally irreversible by simple physical means.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Methods to prevent corrosion of iron include painting, oiling/greasing, galvanising (zinc coating), electroplating, and alloying (e.g. making stainless steel by adding chromium and nickel).

 

• Galvanisation is the process of coating iron/steel with a thin layer of zinc to protect it from rusting.

 

• Tarnishing of silver (turning black due to formation of silver sulphide) and corrosion of copper (forming a green coating of copper carbonate) are other everyday examples.

 

NOTE

 

• Endothermic reaction (Option A): Corrosion actually releases a small amount of energy over time (it is broadly exothermic in nature, though slow); more importantly, this option misidentifies the category entirely — corrosion is a type of chemical change, not simply defined by heat absorption.

 

• Physical change (Option B): Incorrect, since corrosion produces an entirely new chemical substance and is not easily reversible.

 

• Neutralisation reaction (Option C): A neutralisation reaction is specifically an acid reacting with a base to form salt and water — unrelated to the process of corrosion.

question: From the given compounds, which is used as a fuel additive?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethanol.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethanol (C₂H₅OH) is widely used as a fuel additive, blended with petrol (e.g. under India's Ethanol Blended Petrol/EBP programme) to reduce crude-oil consumption and vehicular emissions. (एथेनॉल — पेट्रोल में मिलाया जाने वाला जैव-ईंधन)

 

• Ethanol burns cleanly and, being obtained from renewable sources like sugarcane molasses and grains, is promoted as a biofuel to cut down dependence on fossil fuels.

 

• India has set a target of 20% ethanol blending in petrol (E20), which was achieved ahead of schedule under the National Policy on Biofuels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ethanol is manufactured industrially mainly by the fermentation of sugars (from molasses, grains, etc.) using yeast, followed by distillation.

 

• Ethanol is also the active intoxicating ingredient in alcoholic beverages, and is used as a solvent, in hand sanitizers and in the pharmaceutical industry.

 

• CNG, LPG, biodiesel and hydrogen are other alternative/cleaner fuels used or being promoted in India's transport sector.

 

NOTE

 

• Ethanal (Option A): Also known as acetaldehyde (CH₃CHO); it is an intermediate chemical compound, not used as a fuel additive.

 

• Ethane (Option B): A simple hydrocarbon gas (C₂H₆), a component of natural gas, but not blended with petrol as a fuel additive.

 

• Ethanoic acid (Option D): Commonly known as acetic acid (the acid in vinegar); it is not used as a fuel additive.

question: What is the primary cause of reverberation in a hall or room?
option_2: Absorption of sound by soft materials
option_4: Multiple reflections of sound from hard surfaces
solution_text:
The correct answer is Multiple reflections of sound from hard surfaces.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Reverberation is the persistence (lingering) of sound in a room caused by sound waves bouncing back and forth repeatedly — multiple reflections — off hard surfaces such as bare walls, ceilings and floors before finally dying out. (अनुरणन — कठोर सतहों से बार-बार परावर्तन)

 

• Because each reflection takes some time to travel and return, the reflected sound waves keep arriving at the listener's ear even after the original sound has stopped, making speech or music sound blurred if reverberation is excessive.

 

• Reverberation increases with the hardness and reflectivity of the room's surfaces and decreases when sound-absorbing materials are used.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• To control excessive reverberation, auditoriums and concert halls are lined with sound-absorbent materials such as compressed fibreboard, thick curtains, carpets, and perforated ceiling boards, and seats are often upholstered.

 

• Echo, by contrast, is a distinctly separate repetition of sound, heard when the reflected sound reaches the ear at least 0.1 second after the original sound — it requires a large distance to the reflecting surface (unlike reverberation, which occurs at short distances in enclosed spaces).

 

• Both echo and reverberation are applications of the law of reflection of sound, which is analogous to the law of reflection of light.

 

NOTE

 

• Variation in air temperature (Option A): Affects the speed of sound, not the primary mechanism causing reverberation.

 

• Absorption of sound by soft materials (Option B): This actually reduces reverberation rather than causing it.

 

• Bending of sound waves (Option C): This describes diffraction, a different phenomenon, not the cause of reverberation.

question: Which of the following is considered a major factor contributing to poor living standards in society?
option_1: Inequality in the distribution of resources
option_2: Only the level of education in society
option_3: Overuse of technology in urban areas
option_4: Only the rapid growth of the population
solution_text:
The correct answer is Inequality in the distribution of resources.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Inequality in the distribution of resources — such as income, land, healthcare and education — is widely recognised as a major structural factor contributing to poor living standards, since it leaves large sections of society without adequate access to basic necessities. (संसाधनों के वितरण में असमानता — जीवन स्तर पर प्रभाव)

 

• Living standards depend not only on the total resources a society has, but on how fairly they are shared; even a resource-rich economy can have widespread poverty if wealth is concentrated among a few.

 

• The other options each describe only a single, narrow factor (education alone, or population growth alone), which — taken in isolation — do not capture the broader structural cause targeted by the question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Human Development Index (HDI), published by UNDP, measures living standards using health (life expectancy), education, and per-capita income — reflecting how resource access affects standard of living.

 

• Government programmes such as progressive taxation, subsidies, reservation policies and social welfare schemes aim specifically to reduce resource inequality and improve living standards.

 

• Poverty line estimates in India are based on minimum calorie intake and expenditure needed for a basic standard of living.

 

NOTE

 

• Only the level of education in society (Option B): Education matters, but the word 'only' makes this too narrow to be the general major factor.

 

• Overuse of technology in urban areas (Option C): Not a standard or established cause of poor living standards.

 

• Only the rapid growth of the population (Option D): Population growth can strain resources, but again the word 'only' makes it too narrow compared to the broader structural cause of unequal resource distribution.

question:
An object moves along a straight path from point O to point A (100 m away), then immediately reverses and stops at point B, which is 30 m away from A back towards O.

What is the total distance covered and the magnitude of the displacement, respectively?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 130 m, 70 m.

 

GIVEN

 

• Object moves O → A (100 m), then reverses and moves A → B (30 m, back towards O).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Distance is the total path length actually travelled = O to A + A to B = 100 + 30 = 130 m.

 

• Displacement is the shortest straight-line distance between the initial point (O) and the final point (B), measured with direction. Since B is 30 m back from A (towards O), B is located at 100 − 30 = 70 m from O.

 

• So the magnitude of displacement = 70 m.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Distance always adds up all path segments (100 + 30 = 130 m); displacement is just the net straight-line gap between start and end points (100 − 30 = 70 m), since both legs of the motion are along the same straight line.

 

NOTE

 

• Distance is always ≥ displacement, and distance is always positive (a scalar), while displacement is a vector with both magnitude and direction.

question: The total resistance of 10 resistors of equal resistance R arranged in series arrangement is _____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 10R.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a series combination, resistors are connected end to end so that the same current flows through each one, and their resistances simply add up: R_total = R₁ + R₂ + ... + Rₙ. (श्रेणीक्रम — प्रतिरोधों का योग)

 

• For 10 equal resistors, each of resistance R, connected in series: R_total = R + R + ... (10 times) = 10R.

 

• Series combination always gives a resultant resistance greater than the greatest individual resistance in the combination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a parallel combination, the reciprocal of the equivalent resistance is the sum of reciprocals: 1/R_total = 1/R₁ + 1/R₂ + ... For n equal resistors R in parallel, R_total = R/n.

 

• Series circuits: same current, voltage divides across components; Parallel circuits: same voltage, current divides across branches.

 

• Household electrical circuits are wired in parallel, so that each appliance gets the full voltage and works independently of others.

 

NOTE

 

• R/10 (Option A): This would be the equivalent resistance of 10 equal resistors R connected in parallel, not series.

 

• R10 (Option C): Not a meaningful physical expression; likely a distractor confusing notation.

 

• 10/R (Option D): Has incorrect units/dimensions for resistance and does not follow from either series or parallel formulas.

question: In circuit diagrams, a zigzag line is used to represent which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is A resistor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In standard circuit diagrams, a zigzag line is the conventional symbol used to represent a resistor — a component that opposes/resists the flow of electric current. (प्रतिरोधक — टेढ़ी-मेढ़ी रेखा से दर्शाया जाता है)

 

• A variable resistor (rheostat) is shown as a zigzag line with an arrow drawn diagonally across or touching it, indicating that its resistance value can be changed.

 

• Recognising standard circuit symbols (resistor, cell, switch, ammeter, voltmeter, bulb) is a common basic-science topic tested in competitive exams.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• A cell/battery is represented by two parallel lines of unequal length (long line = positive terminal, short thick line = negative terminal).

 

• A switch (in the open/off position) is shown as a break in the wire with a small gap or a line at an angle; a fuse is usually shown as a small rectangle or oval in the circuit line, sometimes labelled 'F'.

 

• An electric bulb is represented by a circle with a cross or filament symbol inside it.

 

NOTE

 

• A fuse (Option A): Represented by a distinct oval/rectangular symbol in the wire, not a zigzag line.

 

• A switch (Option C): Represented as a break/gap in the circuit with a movable lever symbol, not a zigzag line.

 

• A battery (Option D): Represented by parallel long-and-short lines, not a zigzag line.

question: A runner completes one round of a circular track of radius 175 m in 35 seconds. The average velocity after one round is ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 0 m/s.

 

GIVEN

 

• Circular track of radius = 175 m; runner completes one full round in 35 seconds.

 

SOLUTION

 

• After completing exactly one full round, the runner returns to the exact starting point.

 

• Displacement = shortest distance between initial and final position = 0 (since start and end points coincide).

 

• Average velocity = Displacement ÷ Time = 0 ÷ 35 = 0 m/s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever a body returns to its exact starting point after motion (one complete round of a circle, a round trip, etc.), its displacement is always zero, so its average velocity is always zero, regardless of the distance or speed involved — the radius (175 m) and time (35 s) given here are not even needed for velocity, only for calculating average speed.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse average speed (which would be non-zero here: speed = circumference ÷ time = 2π(175)/35 ≈ 31.4 m/s) with average velocity, which uses displacement, not distance.

question: The Golgi apparatus is associated with which of the following organelles?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Endoplasmic reticulum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Golgi apparatus (Golgi body/complex) works closely with the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) — it receives proteins and lipids synthesised and packaged by the ER (especially the rough ER), then modifies, sorts, packages and dispatches them (via vesicles) to their correct destinations inside or outside the cell. (गॉल्जी उपकरण — अंतर्द्रव्यी जालिका से जुड़ा)

 

• It was discovered by the Italian scientist Camillo Golgi in 1898, and is often called the 'packaging and shipping department' of the cell.

 

• The Golgi apparatus is made of stacked, flattened, membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option B.

 

Additional Information

 

• Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is of two types: rough ER (studded with ribosomes, involved in protein synthesis) and smooth ER (involved in lipid/steroid synthesis and detoxification).

 

• Lysosomes, often called the 'suicide bags' of the cell, are also formed from Golgi apparatus vesicles and contain digestive enzymes.

 

• Mitochondria, the 'powerhouse of the cell', has its own DNA and produces ATP through cellular respiration.

 

NOTE

 

• Mitochondria (Option A): Functions independently in energy (ATP) production; not the organelle most directly linked functionally to the Golgi apparatus.

 

• Plastids (Option C): Found in plant cells (e.g. chloroplasts for photosynthesis); not directly linked to Golgi function.

 

• Nucleus (Option D): Controls cell activities and contains genetic material; while it directs protein synthesis indirectly, it is the ER — not the nucleus — that hands material directly to the Golgi apparatus.

question: Which of the following statements is correct about 'Bohr's model of an Atom'?
option_1: Only certain special orbits known as discrete orbits of electrons are allowed inside the atom.
option_2: While revolving in discrete orbits, the electrons do not exist.
option_3: While revolving in discrete orbits, the electrons radiate energy.
option_4: Only certain special orbits known as discrete orbits of electrons are allowed outside the atom.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only certain special orbits known as discrete orbits of electrons are allowed inside the atom.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Niels Bohr's atomic model (1913) proposed that electrons revolve around the nucleus only in certain fixed, discrete orbits (energy levels/shells), and only these specific orbits are permitted inside the atom — not any arbitrary path. (बोर मॉडल — निश्चित कक्षाओं में इलेक्ट्रॉन)

 

• Electrons revolving in these permitted, stable orbits do not radiate (lose) energy, which is why atoms remain stable under normal conditions — this directly contradicted the earlier prediction of classical physics (which said an accelerating charge must radiate energy).

 

• An electron gains or loses energy — and jumps between orbits — only when it absorbs or emits a photon of a specific energy corresponding exactly to the energy gap between two orbits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bohr's model successfully explained the hydrogen atom's line spectrum, by showing spectral lines correspond to electrons jumping between specific discrete energy levels.

 

• Bohr's model was built upon Rutherford's nuclear model (which established a small, dense, positively charged nucleus) by adding the concept of quantised, stable orbits.

 

• Later, the quantum mechanical model (Schrödinger) refined this further, describing electrons in terms of probability clouds (orbitals) rather than fixed circular paths.

 

NOTE

 

• Option B: Incorrect — electrons do exist while revolving in their orbits; Bohr's model does not claim otherwise.

 

• Option C: Incorrect — this is precisely what Bohr's model denies; electrons in permitted (discrete) orbits do not radiate energy.

 

• Option D: Incorrect — the discrete orbits are permitted paths for electrons that exist around (i.e., 'inside' the overall atomic structure surrounding) the nucleus, not 'outside the atom'.

question: Where should an object be placed in front of a convex lens to get a real image of the size of the object?
option_2: At the principal focus of the lens
option_3: Between infinity and the principal focus of the lens
solution_text:
The correct answer is At twice the focal length.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When an object is placed at the centre of curvature / twice the focal length (2F₁) of a convex lens, the convex lens forms a real, inverted image of the SAME SIZE as the object, also located at 2F₂ on the other side of the lens. (उत्तल लेंस — 2F पर वस्तु रखने पर समान आकार का प्रतिबिम्ब)

 

• This is a standard result from the ray-diagram behaviour of convex lenses, commonly summarised in a table of object-position vs image-characteristics for Class 10 optics.

 

• The image formed here is real (can be captured on a screen) and inverted, but exactly equal in size to the object — neither magnified nor diminished.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Object at infinity → image at focus (F₂), highly diminished, point-sized, real, inverted.

 

• Object beyond 2F₁ → image between F₂ and 2F₂, diminished, real, inverted.

 

• Object between F₁ and the optical centre → image is virtual, erect and magnified, formed on the same side as the object (this is how a convex lens works as a magnifying glass).

 

NOTE

 

• At infinity (Option A): Produces a highly diminished, point-sized image at the focus — not same-sized.

 

• At the principal focus (Option B): Rays emerge parallel after refraction, so the image forms at infinity, highly magnified — not same-sized.

 

• Between infinity and the principal focus (Option C): This broad zone (beyond 2F, or between F and 2F) generally gives images that are diminished or magnified but not exactly the same size — only the specific point 2F gives an image equal in size.

question: What is the chemical formula for Glucose?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C₆H₁₂O₆.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Glucose, a simple monosaccharide sugar, has the molecular formula C₆H₁₂O₆. (ग्लूकोज़ — C₆H₁₂O₆)

 

• It is the primary source of energy for cellular respiration in living organisms, and is the end-product of photosynthesis in green plants (later stored as starch) and of the digestion of carbohydrates in the human body.

 

• Glucose belongs to the class of carbohydrates known as hexose sugars (6-carbon sugars), and is also called dextrose or blood sugar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important sugars: Fructose (C₆H₁₂O₆) — a fruit sugar isomer of glucose; Sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) — table sugar, a disaccharide of glucose + fructose.

 

• The overall equation of photosynthesis is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → (sunlight, chlorophyll) → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.

 

• Cellular respiration is essentially the reverse: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy (ATP).

 

NOTE

 

• C₁₁H₂₂O₁₁ (Option A): Not the correct formula for any common sugar (sucrose is C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁, note the correct carbon count).

 

• CH₃COOH (Option B): This is acetic acid (found in vinegar), not glucose.

 

• CH₄ (Option C): This is methane, a simple hydrocarbon gas, unrelated to glucose.

question:
Neutralisation reaction involves the combination of _________ from the acid and

_________ from the base to form water molecules.
option_1: OH+ ions and H- ions, respectively
option_2: H- ions and OH+ ions, respectively
option_3: OH+ ions and OH- ions, respectively
option_4: H+ ions and OH- ions, respectively
solution_text:
The correct answer is H+ ions and OH- ions, respectively.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A neutralisation reaction is the reaction between an acid and a base, in which the H⁺ ions (from the acid) combine with the OH⁻ ions (from the base) to form water (H₂O), along with a salt. (उदासीनीकरण — H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O)

 

• General equation: Acid + Base → Salt + Water, e.g. HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O.

 

• This reaction is typically exothermic (releases heat) and results in a solution that is closer to neutral (pH nearer 7) than either the original acid or base alone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option D.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acids ionise in water to release H⁺ (hydrogen) ions, giving them a sour taste and the ability to turn blue litmus red.

 

• Bases ionise in water to release OH⁻ (hydroxide) ions, giving them a bitter taste, a soapy feel, and the ability to turn red litmus blue.

 

• Everyday applications of neutralisation include using antacids (a mild base) to relieve acidity in the stomach, and treating acidic soil with lime (calcium compounds, a base).

 

NOTE

 

• Options A, B and C all use the incorrect or non-existent ion notation 'OH+' (hydroxide is OH⁻, an anion, never written as a cation 'OH+'), making them factually and chemically wrong.

question: A passenger standing in a moving bus suddenly falls forward when the bus stops abruptly. This illustrates which of the following laws?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Newton's first law.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Newton's First Law (the Law of Inertia) states that a body continues in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external unbalanced force. (न्यूटन का प्रथम नियम — जड़त्व का नियम)

 

• When the bus is moving, the passenger's body (including their upper body/legs) is also moving at the same speed. When the bus suddenly stops, the passenger's feet stop (as they are in contact with the bus floor), but the rest of the body tends to continue moving forward due to inertia of motion — causing the passenger to lurch/fall forward.

 

• This is a classic real-life illustration of inertia, the tendency of a body to resist any change in its state of motion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Conversely, when a stationary bus suddenly starts moving, standing passengers tend to fall backward, because their body (at rest) resists the sudden forward motion of the bus (inertia of rest).

 

• Newton's Second Law relates force, mass and acceleration: F = ma.

 

• Newton's Third Law states that for every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction (e.g. the recoil of a gun when a bullet is fired).

 

NOTE

 

• Newton's second law (Option B): Concerns the relationship F = ma, not this inertia-based scenario.

 

• Law of gravitation (Option C): Concerns the mutual force of attraction between masses; unrelated to this scenario.

 

• Newton's third law (Option D): Concerns action-reaction force pairs, which is not what is being illustrated here.

question: Which of the following nutrients is required in large quantities by plants?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Phosphorus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Plant nutrients are classified as macronutrients (needed in large quantities) and micronutrients (needed only in trace amounts). Phosphorus is one of the primary macronutrients required by plants in large quantities. (फॉस्फोरस — पौधों के लिए वृहत् पोषक तत्व)

 

• Phosphorus plays a vital role in root development, energy transfer (as part of ATP), and flower/fruit/seed formation in plants.

 

• The three primary macronutrients supplied through common fertilisers are Nitrogen (N), Phosphorus (P) and Potassium (K) — remembered as the 'NPK' of fertilisers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Macronutrients for plants: Carbon, Hydrogen, Oxygen, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium and Sulphur (9 elements needed in relatively large amounts).

 

• Micronutrients for plants: Iron, Zinc, Copper, Manganese, Boron, Molybdenum, Chlorine and Nickel — needed only in very small (trace) quantities, but still essential.

 

• Nitrogen promotes leafy/vegetative growth (chlorophyll formation), while Potassium aids overall plant vigour, disease resistance and water regulation.

 

NOTE

 

• Copper (Option A): A micronutrient, needed only in trace amounts.

 

• Zinc (Option B): A micronutrient, needed only in trace amounts.

 

• Iron (Option D): A micronutrient (needed for chlorophyll synthesis, though not itself a part of chlorophyll), required only in trace amounts, not in large quantities.

question:
Diana is thrice as old as Teresa and Homi is twice as old as Diana. If Diana's age is 4

years less than the average age of all three, then Homi's age (in years) is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 72.

 

GIVEN

 

• Diana = 3 × Teresa; Homi = 2 × Diana; Diana's age = (average age of all three) − 4.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let Teresa's age = t. Then Diana = 3t, and Homi = 2 × 3t = 6t.

 

• Average of all three = (t + 3t + 6t) ÷ 3 = 10t ÷ 3.

 

• Diana = average − 4 ⇒ 3t = 10t/3 − 4. Multiply by 3: 9t = 10t − 12 ⇒ t = 12.

 

• So Teresa = 12, Diana = 36, Homi = 6 × 12 = 72.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Assume Teresa = t, write Diana and Homi directly in terms of t (3t, 6t), form one linear equation from the average condition, and solve for t first — ages then follow instantly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert every relation into a single variable before using the 'average' condition — trying to juggle three unknowns at once leads to errors.

question:
A typist takes 40 minutes to type 2 pages. How long (in minutes) will he take to type 81

pages?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 1620.

 

GIVEN

 

• Time to type 2 pages = 40 minutes.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Time per page = 40 ÷ 2 = 20 minutes/page.

 

• Time for 81 pages = 81 × 20 = 1620 minutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find the unit rate (time for 1 page) first, then simply multiply by the required number of pages: 20 × 81 = 1620.

 

NOTE

 

• This is a direct proportion (more pages ⇒ proportionally more time), so cross-multiplication (2/40 = 81/x) gives the same result.

question:
In a box containing blue, yellow, and orange tokens, the ratio of blue to yellow tokens

was 13 : 19, while the ratio of orange to blue tokens was 10 : 3. What was the ratio of

orange to yellow tokens?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 130 : 57.

 

GIVEN

 

• Blue : Yellow = 13 : 19.

 

• Orange : Blue = 10 : 3, i.e. Blue : Orange = 3 : 10.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Make the 'Blue' term common. Blue appears as 13 in the first ratio and as 3 in the second; LCM(13, 3) = 39.

 

• Blue : Yellow = 13 : 19 → multiply by 3 → 39 : 57.

 

• Blue : Orange = 3 : 10 → multiply by 13 → 39 : 130, i.e. Orange : Blue = 130 : 39.

 

• Now Blue = 39 in both, so combine: Orange : Blue : Yellow = 130 : 39 : 57.

 

• Orange : Yellow = 130 : 57.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• To combine two ratios sharing a common term, scale each ratio so the common term matches (using their LCM), then read off the other two terms directly.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check which term is common between the two given ratios before scaling — here it's 'Blue', which appears on opposite sides in the two ratios.

question: The value of (0.85)³ − (0.1)³ ÷ (0.85)² + 0.085 + 0.01 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 0.75.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: [(0.85)³ − (0.1)³] ÷ [(0.85)² + 0.085 + 0.01].

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let a = 0.85 and b = 0.1. The denominator (0.85)² + 0.085 + 0.01 = a² + ab + b² (since ab = 0.85 × 0.1 = 0.085, and b² = 0.01).

 

• So the expression is exactly of the form (a³ − b³) ÷ (a² + ab + b²).

 

• Using the identity a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²), the (a² + ab + b²) terms cancel, leaving just (a − b).

 

• a − b = 0.85 − 0.1 = 0.75.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever you see (a³ − b³) over (a² + ab + b²), instantly recognise the a³−b³ identity and just compute (a − b) — no need to expand cubes or squares at all.

 

NOTE

 

• Always check the denominator's middle term (here 0.085 = 0.85 × 0.1) to confirm it truly matches the ab term of the identity before cancelling.

question:
For a trip of 600 km, a truck travels the first 300 km at a speed of 42 km/hr. At what

speed (in km/hr) should it cover the remaining distance, so that the average speed for

the entire journey is 63 km/hr?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 126.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total distance = 600 km; first 300 km covered at 42 km/hr; required overall average speed = 63 km/hr.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total time allowed = Total distance ÷ Average speed = 600 ÷ 63 = 200/21 hours.

 

• Time taken for first 300 km = 300 ÷ 42 = 50/7 hours = 150/21 hours.

 

• Time left for remaining 300 km = 200/21 − 150/21 = 50/21 hours.

 

• Required speed = Remaining distance ÷ Remaining time = 300 ÷ (50/21) = 300 × 21/50 = 126 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Always work via total time (distance ÷ average speed), not by averaging the two speeds directly — average speed problems must go through time, since 'average speed' is a distance/time ratio, not an average of speeds.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to simply average 42 and 63 or similar — average speed can NEVER be found by averaging two individual speeds unless the two distances (or times) are equal.

question:
A 435-metre-long train crosses a platform thrice its length in 87 seconds. What is the

speed of the train (in km/hr)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 72.

 

GIVEN

 

• Train length = 435 m; platform length = 3 × 435 = 1305 m; time to cross platform = 87 seconds.

 

SOLUTION

 

• To cross a platform, the train must cover (its own length + the platform's length) = 435 + 1305 = 1740 m.

 

• Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 1740 ÷ 87 = 20 m/s.

 

• Convert to km/hr: 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/hr.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Crosses a platform' always means (train length + platform length) is the distance travelled — a very common trap is to use only the platform length or only the train length.

 

NOTE

 

• To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5; to convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.

question:
A and B working together can do a piece of work in 3 days. B alone can do the same

work in 21 days. How long (in days) will A alone take to do double the work?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 7.

 

GIVEN

 

• (A + B) together finish 1 work in 3 days; B alone finishes it in 21 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• (A + B)'s 1-day work = 1/3. B's 1-day work = 1/21.

 

• A's 1-day work = 1/3 − 1/21 = 7/21 − 1/21 = 6/21 = 2/7.

 

• So A alone takes 7/2 = 3.5 days to finish one work.

 

• To finish double the work, A needs 2 × 3.5 = 7 days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Time for double work = 2 × (time for single work). Once you have A's single-work time (3.5 days here), just double it.

 

NOTE

 

• Always subtract 1-day work rates (not the number of days directly) when combining or separating workers.

question: Simplify: (1 − cos2θ) ÷ sin2θ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. tan θ.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: (1 − cos2θ) ÷ sin2θ.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Use the double-angle identities: 1 − cos2θ = 2sin²θ, and sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ.

 

• Substituting: (2sin²θ) ÷ (2 sinθ cosθ) = sinθ / cosθ = tan θ.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the double-angle forms cos2θ = 1 − 2sin²θ and sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ — most 'simplify the double angle expression' questions collapse quickly once these are substituted.

 

NOTE

 

• Alternatively, put θ = 45° as a quick numeric check: (1 − cos90°)/sin90° = (1−0)/1 = 1 = tan45° ✓, confirming the identity.

question:
If 20% of a number is added to 102, then the result is the same number. 60% of the same

number is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 76.5.

 

GIVEN

 

• 20% of a number, added to 102, gives back the same number.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the number be x. Then 0.2x + 102 = x.

 

• 102 = x − 0.2x = 0.8x ⇒ x = 102 ÷ 0.8 = 127.5.

 

• 60% of x = 0.6 × 127.5 = 76.5.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• '20% of x added to 102 gives x back' simply means 102 is the remaining 80% of x, so x = 102 ÷ 0.8 directly, without needing to set up algebra from scratch each time.

 

NOTE

 

• Always convert 'percentage added/left' statements into a fraction of the whole (here, 102 represents 80% of x) before solving — it's faster and less error-prone than pure algebra.

question: The average of 4, 12, 8, 10, 16, 14, 9, 20, 18, 22, 15 and K is 14. Find the value of K.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 20.

 

GIVEN

 

• 12 values in total: 4, 12, 8, 10, 16, 14, 9, 20, 18, 22, 15 and K; their average = 14.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum of the 11 known numbers = 4+12+8+10+16+14+9+20+18+22+15 = 148.

 

• Since the average of all 12 numbers is 14, total sum = 14 × 12 = 168.

 

• K = Total sum − sum of known numbers = 168 − 148 = 20.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Sum = Average × Count. Compute the total required sum first (average × total count), then subtract the sum of the known values to isolate the unknown.

 

NOTE

 

• Count the terms carefully before starting — miscounting how many values are listed (11 known + K = 12 total here) is the most common mistake in such questions.

question:
Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4,000 at 6% per annum rate of interest for the period

from 21 February 2024 to 22 April 2024.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 40.

 

GIVEN

 

• Principal = ₹4,000; Rate = 6% p.a.; Period = 21 February 2024 to 22 April 2024 (2024 is a leap year).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Number of days: from 21 Feb to 29 Feb (2024, leap year) = 8 days, + full March = 31 days, + up to 22 April = 22 days. Total = 8 + 31 + 22 = 61 days.

 

• Time in years = 61/365.

 

• SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100 = (4000 × 6 × 61) ÷ (100 × 365) = 1,464,000 ÷ 36,500 = ₹40 (approx.).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In date-based SI questions, count days using 'exclude the start date, include the end date' (or vice-versa, but be consistent) and remember leap years have 29 days in February.

 

NOTE

 

• SI = (P×R×T)/100, with T always in years when R is per annum — convert days to years as (days/365) unless the question specifies otherwise.

question:
In a fruit basket, there are twice as many oranges as apples. If there are a total of 36

fruits, how many oranges are there?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 24.

 

GIVEN

 

• Oranges = 2 × Apples; Total fruits = 36.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let apples = x, so oranges = 2x.

 

• x + 2x = 36 ⇒ 3x = 36 ⇒ x = 12.

 

• Oranges = 2 × 12 = 24.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split the total in the ratio given (apples : oranges = 1 : 2, i.e. 3 parts total). 36 ÷ 3 = 12 per part; oranges (2 parts) = 24.

 

NOTE

 

• Always double-check which fruit the question is actually asking for (oranges here, not apples) after finding both values.

question:
The diagonals of a quadrilateral are perpendicular bisectors of each other. If the length

of one diagonal is 8 cm and the area of the quadrilateral is 48 cm², find the length (in

cm) of the other diagonal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 12.

 

GIVEN

 

• A quadrilateral (rhombus) with diagonals perpendicular bisectors of each other; one diagonal d₁ = 8 cm; area = 48 cm².

 

SOLUTION

 

• For a rhombus (diagonals ⊥ bisectors), Area = (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 2.

 

• 48 = (8 × d₂) ÷ 2 = 4 × d₂ ⇒ d₂ = 48 ÷ 4 = 12 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever diagonals are perpendicular bisectors of each other, the figure is a rhombus, and Area = (product of diagonals)/2 — a direct one-step formula.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Perpendicular bisectors of each other' is the defining property of a rhombus (or square); this identification is the key that unlocks the area formula.

question: If x + y + z = 0 and xyz = 21, then x³ + y³ + z³ is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 63.

 

GIVEN

 

• x + y + z = 0 and xyz = 21.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Standard identity: if x + y + z = 0, then x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz.

 

• (This follows because the general identity x³+y³+z³ − 3xyz = (x+y+z)(x²+y²+z²−xy−yz−zx) becomes 0 on the right when x+y+z = 0.)

 

• So x³ + y³ + z³ = 3 × 21 = 63.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever x + y + z = 0 is given, instantly recall x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz — this shortcut appears very frequently in algebra questions.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not confuse this with the case x+y+z ≠ 0, which requires the full identity with the (x²+y²+z²−xy−yz−zx) term.

question: Simplify: [(3⁴ × 9⁻²) ÷ (27⁻¹ × 3⁻³)]^(1/3)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 9.

 

GIVEN

 

• Expression: [(3⁴ × 9⁻²) ÷ (27⁻¹ × 3⁻³)]^(1/3).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Express everything with base 3: 9 = 3², so 9⁻² = 3⁻⁴. Also 27 = 3³, so 27⁻¹ = 3⁻³.

 

• Numerator: 3⁴ × 3⁻⁴ = 3⁰ = 1.

 

• Denominator: 3⁻³ × 3⁻³ = 3⁻⁶.

 

• Fraction = 1 ÷ 3⁻⁶ = 3⁶.

 

• Cube root: (3⁶)^(1/3) = 3^(6/3) = 3² = 9.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every term to the SAME base (here, base 3) first; then use the laws of indices (aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ, aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ, (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ) mechanically — most exponent 'simplify' questions become one-liners this way.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch negative exponents carefully: dividing by a⁻ⁿ is the same as multiplying by aⁿ — a common sign slip-up.

question:
The price per unit of lemon candy to strawberry candy is in the ratio 4 : 14, and a family

consumes them in the ratio 23 : 2 by quantity. Find the ratio of the expenditure on

strawberry candy to that on lemon candy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 7 : 23.

 

GIVEN

 

• Price (per unit): lemon : strawberry = 4 : 14, i.e. lemon = 4k, strawberry = 14k.

 

• Quantity consumed: lemon : strawberry = 23 : 2, i.e. lemon qty = 23m, strawberry qty = 2m.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Expenditure = Price × Quantity.

 

• Expenditure on lemon = 4k × 23m = 92km.

 

• Expenditure on strawberry = 14k × 2m = 28km.

 

• Ratio of (strawberry expenditure) : (lemon expenditure) = 28km : 92km = 7 : 23 (dividing both by 4km).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Expenditure ratio = (price ratio) × (quantity ratio), term by term, matching the same item across both ratios — then simplify.

 

NOTE

 

• Be careful with the order asked: the question wants strawberry-to-lemon, which is the reverse of the order the price ratio was originally given in.

question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 79, 42, 47, 77, 49, 75, 56, 26 and 35 is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 54.

 

GIVEN

 

• 9 observations: 79, 42, 47, 77, 49, 75, 56, 26, 35.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Sum = 79+42+47+77+49+75+56+26+35 = 486.

 

• Number of observations = 9.

 

• Arithmetic mean = Sum ÷ Count = 486 ÷ 9 = 54.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Add numbers in convenient pairs that round to a multiple of 10 (e.g. 79+56... 42+77... etc.) to reduce addition errors when the list is long.

 

NOTE

 

• Always recount the list before dividing — an extra or missing term is the most common source of error in mean questions.

question:
A credit card payment that will settle a bill for 290 microwaves at ₹1,050 per microwave

with successive discounts of 4% and 25%, with a further discount of 5% on card

payment is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹2,08,278.

 

GIVEN

 

• 290 microwaves × ₹1,050 each; successive discounts of 4%, 25%, and a further 5% (card payment).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Total marked price = 290 × 1050 = ₹3,04,500.

 

• After 4% discount: 3,04,500 × 0.96 = ₹2,92,320.

 

• After 25% discount: 2,92,320 × 0.75 = ₹2,19,240.

 

• After 5% discount (card): 2,19,240 × 0.95 = ₹2,08,278.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For successive discounts, multiply the price by (1 − each discount) one after another — never simply add the discount percentages together (4+25+5 = 34% is WRONG; the true combined effect is smaller).

 

NOTE

 

• Apply the discounts strictly in the order they are given, one on the reduced price from the previous step, not on the original price each time.

question:
P is any point inside the rectangle ABCD. If PA = 57 cm, PB = 9 cm, and PC = 54 cm,

then the length PD (in cm) is equal to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 78.

 

GIVEN

 

• P is any point inside rectangle ABCD; PA = 57 cm, PB = 9 cm, PC = 54 cm.

 

SOLUTION

 

• By the British Flag Theorem, for any point P inside a rectangle ABCD: PA² + PC² = PB² + PD².

 

• PA² + PC² = 57² + 54² = 3249 + 2916 = 6165.

 

• PB² + PD² = 6165 ⇒ 81 + PD² = 6165 ⇒ PD² = 6084.

 

• PD = √6084 = 78 cm.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Memorise the British Flag Theorem directly: PA² + PC² = PB² + PD² for any point inside a rectangle, where A & C, and B & D, are pairs of OPPOSITE corners — it turns this into a one-line calculation.

 

NOTE

 

• Make sure to pair up the correct OPPOSITE vertices (A opposite C, B opposite D) — pairing adjacent vertices instead will give a wrong equation.

question:
A shop that sells towels has offers going on, wherein customers can buy 2 towels and

get 2 free. What is the percentage discount that customers get?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 50%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Offer: buy 2 towels, get 2 more free (i.e. pay for 2, take home 4 in total).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Customer pays for 2 towels but receives 4 towels — i.e. gets 2 free out of 4 total.

 

• Discount % = (value of free items ÷ value of total items received) × 100 = (2 ÷ 4) × 100 = 50%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 'buy m get n free' offers, discount % = [n ÷ (m+n)] × 100. Here m = 2, n = 2, so discount = 2/4 × 100 = 50%.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not calculate discount as (free items ÷ paid items) — it must be (free items ÷ TOTAL items received), since discount is always a percentage of the total value.

question:
A cylindrical water tank has a diameter of 2.8 m and a height of 3.5 m. It is to be painted

on both its outer curved surface and two circular ends. If the cost of painting is ₹25/m²,

find the total cost of painting the tank. (Use π = 22/7)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. ₹1,078.

 

GIVEN

 

• Diameter = 2.8 m ⇒ radius r = 1.4 m; height h = 3.5 m; cost of painting = ₹25/m²; π = 22/7.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Curved surface area (CSA) = 2πrh = 2 × 22/7 × 1.4 × 3.5 = 2 × 22/7 × 4.9 = 2 × 15.4 = 30.8 m².

 

• Area of the two circular ends = 2 × πr² = 2 × 22/7 × 1.4² = 2 × 22/7 × 1.96 = 2 × 6.16 = 12.32 m².

 

• Total area to be painted = 30.8 + 12.32 = 43.12 m².

 

• Total cost = 43.12 × 25 = ₹1,078.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'Painted on both the curved surface and the two circular ends' means the TOTAL surface area of a cylinder is needed: TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² = 2πr(h + r). Compute that once, then multiply by the rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Always halve the given diameter to get the radius before substituting into any cylinder formula — using diameter directly is a very common mistake.

question:
The cost of 1 litre milk is equal to the selling price of 800 ml milk. The percentage of

profit is ____.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 25%.

 

GIVEN

 

• Cost price of 1000 ml (1 litre) milk = Selling price of 800 ml milk (same rupee amount).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Let the price be ₹1 per ml. Then CP of 1000 ml = ₹1000, and this same ₹1000 is the SP for only 800 ml.

 

• In effect, the seller gives less quantity (800 ml) for the cost-price-value of 1000 ml, making a profit.

 

• Profit = CP(equivalent 1000 ml) − actual quantity sold's cost = the seller effectively gains on (1000 − 800) = 200 ml worth, relative to 800 ml.

 

• Profit % = (1000 − 800) ÷ 800 × 100 = 200 ÷ 800 × 100 = 25%.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Whenever 'cost of X equals selling price of Y' (X > Y) is given, Profit % = [(X − Y) ÷ Y] × 100 directly — here (1000−800)/800 × 100 = 25%.

 

NOTE

 

• Always divide by the SMALLER (actual quantity sold, Y = 800 ml here) as the base for profit %, since profit/loss % is always calculated on the cost/selling price actually incurred, not on the larger reference quantity.

question:
At beginning of the poll, Rahul received 52% of the total votes and Leena received 48%

of the total votes. The total voting was of 3,72,000 votes. How many votes did Leena

earn above 1,00,000?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 78,560 votes.

 

GIVEN

 

• Total votes = 3,72,000; Leena received 48% of the total votes.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Leena's votes = 48% of 3,72,000 = 0.48 × 3,72,000 = 1,78,560 votes.

 

• Votes above 1,00,000 = 1,78,560 − 1,00,000 = 78,560 votes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Compute the required percentage first (Leena's actual vote count), THEN subtract the reference number (1,00,000) asked in the question — don't mix the percentage step and subtraction step together.

 

NOTE

 

• Option A (1,78,560) is simply Leena's total votes — a distractor for those who forget to subtract 1,00,000 as the question actually asks.

question:
Akriti earns ₹ 54,500 monthly and saves 17% of her salary. Find her monthly

expenditure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. ₹45,235.

 

GIVEN

 

• Monthly salary = ₹54,500; savings = 17% of salary.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Savings = 17% of 54,500 = 0.17 × 54,500 = ₹9,265.

 

• Expenditure = Salary − Savings = 54,500 − 9,265 = ₹45,235.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Since savings + expenditure = 100% of salary, expenditure directly = (100% − 17%) of salary = 83% of 54,500 = 45,235 — a one-step calculation avoiding a separate subtraction.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch out for close-looking distractor options (₹45,325, ₹45,523, ₹45,352) — these are digit-rearrangements of the correct answer, designed to catch calculation slips.

question:
Three men can dig a well 39 feet deep in 4 days. How many men can dig a well 78 feet

deep in 12 days?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 2.

 

GIVEN

 

• 3 men dig a 39-feet-deep well in 4 days.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Using (Men × Days) ÷ Depth = constant (work rate per unit depth): (3 × 4) ÷ 39 = 12/39 = 4/13 men-days per foot.

 

• For a 78-feet well in 12 days: Men × 12 ÷ 78 = 4/13 ⇒ Men = (4/13) × (78/12) = (4 × 78) ÷ (13 × 12) = 312 ÷ 156 = 2.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Set up (M₁D₁)/W₁ = (M₂D₂)/W₂ for 'men-days proportional to work (depth dug)' questions — a direct one-equation solve, much faster than reasoning in words.

 

NOTE

 

• 78 feet is exactly double 39 feet, so intuitively: if 3 men take 4 days for 39 feet, digging double the depth in triple the days (12 days = 3×4) needs only 2/3 as many men-per-day-unit, i.e., fewer men than 3 — confirming 2 is reasonable.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

921 923 927 933 941 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 951.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 921, 923, 927, 933, 941, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Find the differences between consecutive terms: 923−921=2; 927−923=4; 933−927=6; 941−933=8.

 

• The differences themselves increase by 2 each time: 2, 4, 6, 8, so the next difference = 10.

 

• Next term = 941 + 10 = 951.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For number series, always write the differences between consecutive terms on a second line first — an evenly increasing/decreasing difference pattern (like +2, +4, +6, +8...) is usually the key.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check the difference pattern using at least 3-4 consecutive gaps before applying it forward, to avoid mistaking a coincidence for the real rule.

question:
Select the triad that follows the same pattern as the one followed by the two triads

given below. Both triads follow the same pattern.

 

LF-OI-RT

NH-QK-TV
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. PJ-SM-VX.

 

GIVEN

 

• Example triads: LF-OI-RT and NH-QK-TV, both following the same hidden pattern.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Look at the FIRST letters of each triad: in LF-OI-RT, they are L(12), O(15), R(18) — each +3. In NH-QK-TV, they are N(14), Q(17), T(20) — each +3 too.

 

• Look at the SECOND letters: in LF-OI-RT, they are F(6), I(9), T(20) — steps of +3, then +11. In NH-QK-TV, they are H(8), K(11), V(22) — steps of +3, then +11 too. Both patterns match consistently.

 

• Now test option C, PJ-SM-VX: first letters P(16), S(19), V(22) — steps of +3, +3 ✓. Second letters J(10), M(13), X(24) — steps of +3, +11 ✓. Both conditions satisfied.

 

• Checking the other options: A and B have first-letter steps of +4, +3 (fails); D has second-letter steps of +3, +12 (fails, should be +11).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split each triad's first letters and second letters into two separate mini-series, find each series' step pattern from the two given examples, then check which option matches BOTH patterns simultaneously.

 

NOTE

 

• A close look-alike option often gets just ONE of the two letter-columns right — always verify both columns before finalising the answer.

question:
Refer to the number series given below and answer the question that follows. Counting

to be done from left to right only.

(NOTE: All numbers are single-digit numbers only.)

 

(Left) 5 2 7 5 4 7 9 8 5 3 6 2 1 5 7 4 9 7 2 5 2 4 3 7 8 4 7 (Right)

 

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an even

digit and also immediately followed by an even digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series (27 digits): 5 2 7 5 4 7 9 8 5 3 6 2 1 5 7 4 9 7 2 5 2 4 3 7 8 4 7

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan left to right, checking every odd digit for an even digit immediately before AND an even digit immediately after it.

 

• Going through the series, the only such position is the segment '...9 7 2 5 2...' — specifically the '5' that appears just after '2, 4' — precisely: '...2 5 2...' where the odd digit 5 is preceded by even 2 and followed by even 2.

 

• Checking every other odd digit in the string (there are many 5s, 7s, 9s, 1s, 3s), each one fails the test because at least one neighbour is odd, not even — for instance the first '5' at position 1 has no left neighbour, and most interior odd digits sit next to another odd digit.

 

• Only one odd digit satisfies the full condition (even-odd-even).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every EVEN digit in the string first; a qualifying odd digit must sit strictly between two underlined (even) digits — this visual filter is much faster than checking each digit's neighbours from memory.

 

NOTE

 

• The very first and very last digits of the series can never qualify, since they have no digit on one side — always exclude the two end positions from your count.

question:
Seven people, A, B, C, D, E, F, and G, are sitting in a row, facing the north. Only two

people sit to the left of A. Only three people sit between A and G. D sits second to the

right of A. Only two people sit between D and C. E sits at some place to the right of F

but at some place to the left of B.

How many people sit to the right of C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 5.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people A-G in a row facing north; only 2 sit left of A; only 3 sit between A & G; D is 2nd to the right of A; only 2 sit between D & C; F is left of E, and E is left of B.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 'Only two people sit to the left of A' ⇒ A is at position 3 (from the left).

 

• 'Only three people sit between A and G' ⇒ G is 4 places from A ⇒ G is at position 7.

 

• 'D sits second to the right of A' ⇒ D = position 3 + 2 = position 5.

 

• 'Only two people sit between D and C' ⇒ C is 3 places from D (position 5); position 8 doesn't exist, so C = 5 − 3 = position 2.

 

• Remaining positions 1, 4, 6 are for B, E, F. Since F is left of E, and E is left of B, the only order fitting these leftover slots is F=1, E=4, B=6.

 

• Final seating (left to right): F, C, A, E, D, B, G.

 

• People to the right of C (position 2): positions 3-7 = A, E, D, B, G = 5 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In linear arrangement puzzles, fix the absolute positions given directly by 'Xth from left/right' clues first, then use the relative clues (only for/between) to place the rest — absolute clues anchor the whole row fastest.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Only N people sit between X and Y' always gives TWO possible positions for Y (N+1 places to either side of X) — always check whether the row length rules one of them out, as it did here for C.

question:
Ronak starts from Point A and drives 6 km towards the south. He then takes a left turn,

drives 5 km, turns left and drives 14 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 11 km. He

takes a final left turn, drives 8 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and

towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are

90-degree turns only unless specified.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 6 km to the east.

 

GIVEN

 

• Path: South 6 km → Left turn, East 5 km → Left turn, North 14 km → Left turn, West 11 km → Left turn, South 8 km, stop at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take East = +x, North = +y. Start at A = (0, 0).

 

• South 6 km: (0, −6). Facing south, a left turn points east; drive 5 km east: (5, −6).

 

• Facing east, a left turn points north; drive 14 km north: (5, 8).

 

• Facing north, a left turn points west; drive 11 km west: (−6, 8).

 

• Facing west, a left turn points south; drive 8 km south: P = (−6, 0).

 

• P is 6 km to the west of A (since A = (0,0) and P = (−6,0)). So, to return from P to A, Ronak must travel 6 km in the opposite direction, i.e. 6 km to the east.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Plot each leg on a simple mental (or rough) x-y grid, always turning left consistently (South→East→North→West→South...), then just read off the net (x, y) offset of the final point from the start — the return path is simply the reverse vector.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Left turn' direction depends on current facing direction — always re-derive it fresh at each step (S→E→N→W→S... in a consistent 90° rotation) rather than assuming a fixed compass shift.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information

given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly

known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the

statements.

 

Statements: All geysers are lights. No light is an oven.

 

Conclusion (I): No geyser is an oven.

Conclusion (II): Some ovens are lights.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Only conclusion (I) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• Statements: All geysers are lights (Geyser ⊆ Light). No light is an oven (Light ∩ Oven = ∅).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Conclusion (I): No geyser is an oven. Since every geyser is a light, and no light is an oven, no geyser can be an oven either — this is a valid syllogistic deduction (All A are B + No B is C ⇒ No A is C). Conclusion (I) follows.

 

• Conclusion (II): Some ovens are lights. The statement 'No light is an oven' means there is ZERO overlap between lights and ovens at all — so it is impossible for 'some ovens' to be lights. Conclusion (II) does not follow (it directly contradicts the given statement).

 

• Hence, only Conclusion (I) follows.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Draw quick Venn diagrams: 'All A are B' = circle A fully inside circle B; 'No B is C' = circles B and C completely separate. Read off conclusions directly from the resulting diagram instead of reasoning purely verbally.

 

NOTE

 

• A universal negative statement ('No X is Y') can NEVER validly produce a 'Some' conclusion about X and Y being related — that would need at least a partial overlap, which a universal negative explicitly rules out.

question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers

are single digit numbers only). (Counting to be done from left to right only.)

 

(Left) 6 3 1 1 2 3 2 8 5 7 6 1 3 7 2 6 9 6 9 2 4 6 2 8 6 3 1 (Right)

 

How many such even numbers are there each of which is immediately preceded by an

odd number and also immediately followed by an odd number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 3.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series (27 digits): 6 3 1 1 2 3 2 8 5 7 6 1 3 7 2 6 9 6 9 2 4 6 2 8 6 3 1

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for even digits with an ODD digit immediately before AND an ODD digit immediately after.

 

• 1st qualifying spot: '...1 3 2 3...' (5th digit '2', preceded by odd 3, followed by odd 3).

 

• 2nd qualifying spot: '...7 6 1...' (11th digit '6', preceded by odd 7, followed by odd 1).

 

• 3rd qualifying spot: '...9 6 9...' (18th digit '6', preceded by odd 9, followed by odd 9).

 

• No other even digit in the series has odd numbers on BOTH sides, giving a total of 3 qualifying digits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Circle every ODD digit first; any EVEN digit sandwiched directly between two circled digits automatically qualifies — scan the string once with this visual filter instead of checking neighbours digit-by-digit from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• Remember the boundary rule: the first and last digits of the series can never qualify since one side has no neighbour at all.

question:
A, B, C, E, F, P and Q are sitting around a circular table, facing the centre. F sits third to

the left of C. Only one person sits between C and P when counted from the left of P.

Only two people sit between B and E when counted from the right of E. A is an

immediate neighbour of B. Who sits to the immediate left and right of Q, respectively?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. C and P.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A, B, C, E, F, P, Q) around a circular table, facing the centre.

 

• F is 3rd to the left of C; only 1 person sits between C and P (counted from the left of P); only 2 people sit between B and E (counted from the right of E); A is an immediate neighbour of B.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix C at a reference position. 'F sits third to the left of C' places F three seats to the left of C.

 

• 'Only one person sits between C and P, counted from the left of P' places C two seats to the left of P (i.e. moving left from P, one person, then C) — so effectively C and P end up as neighbours-once-removed of each other via F, with the arrangement working out to seat Q exactly between C and P on the remaining open seat.

 

• Using the B–E clue (2 people between them, counted from the right of E) and 'A is an immediate neighbour of B' to place the last three people (A, B, E) into the remaining seats, the only fully consistent circular arrangement leaves Q flanked directly by C on one side and P on the other.

 

• Hence the immediate left and right of Q are C and P respectively.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In circular-table puzzles with 'left of X' / 'right of X' phrasing, fix ONE person's seat as your reference (e.g. seat C at 12 o'clock) and consistently apply one rotation direction for 'left' throughout — mixing directions mid-solution is the most common cause of errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Always place the absolute/counted clues (third to the left, only one person between) before the purely relative clues (immediate neighbour, not a neighbour) — the counted clues fix positions uniquely, while relative clues merely narrow down remaining options.

question:
In the following triads, each group of letters is related to the subsequent one following a

certain logic. Select from the given options, the one which follows the same logic.

 

WEST - EWST - WSTE

TOPS - OTPS - TPSO
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. EXIT - XEIT - EITX.

 

GIVEN

 

• WEST → EWST → WSTE, and TOPS → OTPS → TPSO both follow the same hidden transformation rule.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Step 1 (word → 2nd word): the first two letters are swapped. WEST (W,E,S,T) → swap W,E → EWST ✓. TOPS (T,O,P,S) → swap T,O → OTPS ✓.

 

• Step 2 (2nd word → 3rd word): the first letter of the 2nd word is moved to the end. EWST → remove E, append at end → WSTE ✓. OTPS → remove O, append at end → TPSO ✓.

 

• Apply the same two steps to each option's first word:

 

• Option D: EXIT (E,X,I,T) → swap first two (E,X) → XEIT (matches the given middle term) → move first letter X to the end → EITX (matches the given last term). Both steps check out perfectly.

 

• The other options fail at least one of the two steps when checked the same way.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK
