• Break any 'word transformation' series into two isolated micro-rules (compare word1→word2, then word2→word3) using the GIVEN examples first; then test each option against BOTH micro-rules independently rather than guessing the whole pattern at once.

 

NOTE

 

• Watch for options that satisfy the FIRST transformation step correctly but break at the second — always verify both steps, not just the first.

question:
Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as are the numbers of

the following sets.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down

the numbers into their constituent digits. E.g. 13 – Operations on 13 such as adding

to/subtracting from/multiplying with 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and

3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed.)

 

(34, 70, 1)

(21, 92, 25)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. (17, 52, 9).

 

GIVEN

 

• Example sets: (34, 70, 1) and (21, 92, 25).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Test the relation: middle number = 2 × (first number + third number).

 

• Check (34, 70, 1): 2 × (34 + 1) = 2 × 35 = 70 ✓.

 

• Check (21, 92, 25): 2 × (21 + 25) = 2 × 46 = 92 ✓. Pattern confirmed.

 

• Now test each option with the same rule: Option D (17, 52, 9): 2 × (17 + 9) = 2 × 26 = 52 ✓. It matches exactly.

 

• Checking the others: A gives 2×(36+1)=74≠73; B gives 2×(2+14)=32≠31; C gives 2×(19+13)=64≠63 — all fail.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For 3-number-set analogy questions, first hunt for a relation between the FIRST and THIRD numbers that produces the MIDDLE number (sum, product, difference) — the middle term is usually the 'result' term.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly disallows digit-splitting (e.g. splitting 13 into 1 and 3) — always work with the whole numbers as single values.

question:
If ‘A’ stands for ‘+’, ‘B’ stands for ‘−’, ‘C’ stands for ‘÷’ and ‘D’ stands for ‘×’, what will

come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?

 

75 B 4 D 20 A 40 C 8 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 0.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: A = '+', B = '−', C = '÷', D = '×'. Equation: 75 B 4 D 20 A 40 C 8 = ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace the letters with their actual symbols: 75 − 4 × 20 + 40 ÷ 8 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS (÷ and × before + and −): 4 × 20 = 80; 40 ÷ 8 = 5.

 

• Now compute: 75 − 80 + 5 = −5 + 5 = 0.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First substitute all the coded letters with their real symbols in one pass, THEN apply BODMAS normally — trying to do both steps together often causes order-of-operations mistakes.

 

NOTE

 

• Always re-check the letter-to-symbol key given at the start of the question before substituting — these codes are frequently designed to NOT match the alphabetical/intuitive order (as here, where B = '−' and D = '×').

question:
Select the pair that follows the same pattern as that followed by the two pairs given

below. Both pairs follow the same pattern.

AWY−UQS

RNP−LHJ
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. PLN−JFH.

 

GIVEN

 

• Example pairs: AWY → UQS, and RNP → LHJ, both following the same letter-shift rule.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Compare each letter position: A(1)→U(21): a shift of −6 (mod 26, i.e. subtract 6, wrapping around). W(23)→Q(17): −6. Y(25)→S(19): −6. All three letters shift by −6.

 

• Verify with the second pair: R(18)→L(12): −6. N(14)→H(8): −6. P(16)→J(10): −6. Confirmed: every letter shifts back by exactly 6 places.

 

• Apply the same '−6' rule to option A's first term, PLN: P(16)−6=10=J; L(12)−6=6=F; N(14)−6=8=H. This gives JFH, exactly matching the given second term.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert letters to numbers (A=1...Z=26), find the constant shift from the FIRST worked example, confirm it with the SECOND example, then apply that single number directly to each option — much faster than eyeballing letter patterns.

 

NOTE

 

• If a shift value goes below 1, wrap around cyclically by adding 26 (e.g. a shift that would give 0 or negative becomes 26 or 26+that value) — though it isn't needed in this particular question.

question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information

given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly

known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the

statements.

 

Statements:

All lotions are creams.

All creams are soaps.

No cream is a facewash.

 

Conclusions:

(I) No soap is a facewash.

(II) No lotion is a facewash.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Only conclusion (II) follows.

 

GIVEN

 

• All lotions are creams (Lotion ⊆ Cream). All creams are soaps (Cream ⊆ Soap). No cream is a facewash (Cream ∩ Facewash = ∅).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Conclusion (II): No lotion is a facewash. Since all lotions are creams, and no cream is a facewash, no lotion can be a facewash either (All A are B + No B is C ⇒ No A is C). Conclusion (II) follows.

 

• Conclusion (I): No soap is a facewash. We only know 'all creams are soaps' (Cream is a SUBSET of Soap) — this tells us nothing about soaps that are NOT creams; those soaps could well be facewashes. So we cannot validly conclude that NO soap at all is a facewash. Conclusion (I) does not follow.

 

• Hence, only Conclusion (II) is a valid deduction.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Watch the DIRECTION of the subset relationship carefully: 'No cream is a facewash' only rules out facewash for the SMALLER set (cream) and anything fully inside it (lotion) — it says nothing about the LARGER set (soap), which may contain other elements outside 'cream'.

 

NOTE

 

• A very common trap: assuming a property of a subset (cream) automatically applies to its superset (soap) — it only applies the other way around.

question:
A, B, C, R, S, T and U are sitting around a circular table facing the centre of the table.

Only one person sits between S and T when counted from the left of T. R sits third to the

right of A. U sits third to the left of C. R sits to the immediate right of U. B is not an

immediate neighbour of U. How many people sit between B and T when counted from

the right of B?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• 7 people (A, B, C, R, S, T, U) around a circular table facing the centre.

 

• Only 1 person between S & T (counted from left of T); R is 3rd to the right of A; U is 3rd to the left of C; R is immediate right of U; B is NOT an immediate neighbour of U.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Fix A's seat as the reference. 'R sits third to the right of A' places R three seats to the right of A.

 

• 'U sits third to the left of C', combined with 'R sits to the immediate right of U', pins down U and hence R relative to C.

 

• Placing S and T using 'only one person sits between S and T, counted from the left of T' fixes their seats, and the final open seat goes to B — checking 'B is not an immediate neighbour of U' confirms which of the two otherwise-possible seats B actually takes.

 

• Working through the full seating this way, the unique valid circular arrangement (going around) comes out as: A, S, C, B, R, U, T (in order).

 

• Counting from B towards T going through C, S, A (i.e. counted from the right of B, the direction away from R/U): the people sitting between B and T are C, S and A — a total of 3 people.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Place all the ABSOLUTE/counted clues (third to the right/left, only one person between) on the circle first — they pin down 4-5 seats immediately — and use the relative/negative clues (not a neighbour) only at the very end, to break the final tie.

 

NOTE

 

• In circular arrangements, always double check whether 'left' and 'right' are being measured from the point of view of a person FACING the centre (as here) — this reverses the usual clockwise/anticlockwise sense compared to people facing outward.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

161 165 173 185 201 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 221.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 161, 165, 173, 185, 201, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Differences between consecutive terms: 165−161=4; 173−165=8; 185−173=12; 201−185=16.

 

• The differences increase by 4 each time: 4, 8, 12, 16, so the next difference = 20.

 

• Next term = 201 + 20 = 221.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Once you see the differences forming their own arithmetic progression (here, increasing by a constant 4), just extend that secondary series by one more step to find the next main-series difference.

 

NOTE

 

• These 'difference of differences is constant' series are effectively quadratic (second-order arithmetic) series — a very common RRB pattern.

question:
In a row of 50 students facing north, Neetu is 12th from the right end. If Kaden is 6th to

the left of Neetu, what is Kaden's position from the left end of the line?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 33rd.

 

GIVEN

 

• Row of 50 students; Neetu is 12th from the right end; Kaden is 6th to the left of Neetu.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Neetu's position from the LEFT end = Total − (position from right) + 1 = 50 − 12 + 1 = 39th from the left.

 

• Kaden is 6th to the left of Neetu, so Kaden's position from the left = Neetu's position − 6 = 39 − 6 = 33rd from the left.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert ANY 'from the right' position to 'from the left' immediately using: (Total + 1 − position from right), then do all further left/right shifting in that single consistent frame of reference.

 

NOTE

 

• A common mistake is to forget the '+1' in the conversion formula (Total − position + 1) — always include it, since both ends are counted as position 1 from their respective sides.

question:
In a particular coding system, 'house' is represented as '35791' and 'hose' is encoded as

'3751'. How is 'u' represented in this coding system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 9.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'house' → '35791'; 'hose' → '3751'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The code works by alphabetical rank within the word: write the word's letters in alphabetical order, and the code digits (in the order they are written, 1st, 2nd, 3rd...) are assigned to that alphabetically-sorted sequence — the smallest letter gets the smallest odd digit(1), the next gets the next odd digit(3), and so on.

 

• For 'house' (h, o, u, s, e): alphabetically sorted, the letters are e, h, o, s, u. Matching them, in order, to the code's digits 1, 3, 5, 7, 9: e=1, h=3, o=5, s=7, u=9.

 

• Cross-check with 'hose' (h, o, s, e): alphabetically sorted e, h, o, s ↔ code digits 1, 3, 5, 7: e=1, h=3, o=5, s=7 — consistent with the values found from 'house' (h=3, o=5, s=7 match exactly in both words).

 

• So the code for 'u' = 9.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• In letter-coding puzzles, if reading the code digits straight against the word's original letter order gives inconsistent results for a repeated letter (as it does here), the code is almost certainly based on the word's letters sorted ALPHABETICALLY rather than their original position.

 

NOTE

 

• Always verify your decoding rule against BOTH given example words (using their common letters h, o, s, e here) before applying it to find the unknown letter's code.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are

alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which is the letter-cluster that DOES NOT

belong to that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. UWR.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-clusters: QRN, UWR, STP, WXT.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert each letter to its alphabet position and find the step pattern between consecutive letters:

 

• QRN: Q(17)→R(18) = +1; R(18)→N(14) = −4. Pattern: (+1, −4).

 

• STP: S(19)→T(20) = +1; T(20)→P(16) = −4. Pattern: (+1, −4).

 

• WXT: W(23)→X(24) = +1; X(24)→T(20) = −4. Pattern: (+1, −4).

 

• UWR: U(21)→W(23) = +2; W(23)→R(18) = −5. Pattern: (+2, −5) — this breaks the (+1, −4) pattern shared by the other three.

 

Therefore, UWR does not belong to the group, matching Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert every letter-cluster to number form and write down the step (difference) between each consecutive pair; three clusters sharing the identical step-pattern instantly reveal the odd one out.

 

NOTE

 

• The question explicitly warns the pattern is NOT about vowel/consonant count or position — so always default to checking numeric alphabet-position steps for such letter-cluster odd-one-out questions.

question:
In a row of people all facing north, Hirani is 17th from the left end, and Tushar is 32th

from the left end. Tushar is exactly between Hirani and Kiran. If Kiran is 12th from the

right end of the line, how many people are there in the row?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 58.

 

GIVEN

 

• Hirani = 17th from left; Tushar = 32nd from left; Tushar is exactly midway between Hirani and Kiran; Kiran = 12th from the right end.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Tushar is exactly between Hirani (position 17) and Kiran, so the distance from Hirani to Tushar equals the distance from Tushar to Kiran.

 

• Distance from Hirani to Tushar = 32 − 17 = 15 positions.

 

• So Kiran's position from the left = Tushar's position + 15 = 32 + 15 = 47th from the left.

 

• Kiran is also given as 12th from the right end. Using Total = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1:

 

• Total = 47 + 12 − 1 = 58.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• 'X is exactly between A and B' means X's position is the midpoint, so the gap on either side of X is equal — use this to find the third person's position by simple addition/subtraction, then apply Total = (left position) + (right position) − 1 to get the row length.

 

NOTE

 

• Always subtract 1 (not add) in the Total = left + right − 1 formula, since the counted person is included in BOTH the 'from left' and 'from right' counts.

question:
Each of the digits in the number 4876231 is arranged in ascending order from left to

right. What will be the sum of the digits which are second from the left and third from

the right in the new number thus formed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 8.

 

GIVEN

 

• Number: 4876231 (digits: 4, 8, 7, 6, 2, 3, 1).

 

SOLUTION

 

• Arrange the digits in ascending order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8.

 

• Second digit from the left = 2.

 

• Third digit from the right: counting from the right (8 is 1st, 7 is 2nd, 6 is 3rd) = 6.

 

• Sum = 2 + 6 = 8.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• After sorting, write the digits out fully and number them from BOTH ends (1st, 2nd, 3rd... from left AND from right) before picking out the required positions — this avoids miscounting from the wrong end.

 

NOTE

 

• Double-check that all 7 digits of the original number were carried over correctly into the sorted list — a dropped or duplicated digit is the most common error here.

question:
Based on the English alphabetical order, three of the following four letter-clusters are

alike in a certain way and thus form a group. Which letter-cluster DOES NOT belong to

that group?

(Note: The odd one out is not based on the number of consonants/vowels or their

position in the letter-cluster.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. LOI.

 

GIVEN

 

• Four letter-clusters: LOI, HKF, ILG, QTO.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Convert each letter to its alphabet position and find the step pattern:

 

• HKF: H(8)→K(11) = +3; K(11)→F(6) = −5. Pattern: (+3, −5).

 

• ILG: I(9)→L(12) = +3; L(12)→G(7) = −5. Pattern: (+3, −5).

 

• QTO: Q(17)→T(20) = +3; T(20)→O(15) = −5. Pattern: (+3, −5).

 

• LOI: L(12)→O(15) = +3; O(15)→I(9) = −6. Pattern: (+3, −6) — breaks the (+3, −5) pattern shared by the other three.

 

Therefore, LOI does not belong to the group, matching Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Convert each letter-cluster into alphabet-position numbers and compute consecutive differences; the odd one out will differ in just ONE of the two steps — spot it by comparing all four side by side.

 

NOTE

 

• Always compute BOTH steps of each 3-letter cluster (1st→2nd AND 2nd→3rd) — checking only the first step can wrongly eliminate the real answer.

question:
In a certain code language, ‘PEARL’ is coded as ‘18723’ and ‘PAYER’ is coded as

‘82736’. What is the code for ‘Y’ in the given code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. 6.

 

GIVEN

 

• 'PEARL' → '18723'; 'PAYER' → '82736'.

 

SOLUTION

 

• The code digits correspond to the word's letters sorted alphabetically, in the SAME left-to-right order the digits are printed.

 

• Word 'PAYER' has letters P, A, Y, E, R. Sorted alphabetically: A, E, P, R, Y.

 

• Match these, in order, to the given code digits '8, 2, 7, 3, 6': A=8, E=2, P=7, R=3, Y=6.

 

• (As a partial check, the letter R also appears in 'PEARL', where the same rule gives a consistent value, confirming the sorted-order coding method being used.)

 

Therefore, the code for 'Y' = 6, matching Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Find the letter's rank when the WORD'S OWN letters are arranged alphabetically (Y is the 5th/last letter alphabetically among P,A,Y,E,R), then simply pick the digit occupying that same rank-position in the GIVEN code string (read left to right, not re-sorted).

 

NOTE

 

• Do NOT assume the code digits align with the word's letters in their ORIGINAL left-to-right spelling order — as seen here, that gives inconsistent results; the digits align with the alphabetically-sorted letter order instead.

question:
This question is based on the five, three-digit numbers given below.

 

(Left) 567 862 426 326 749 (Right)

 

(Example: 697 – First digit = 6, second digit = 9 and third digit = 7)

(NOTE: All operations to be done from left to right.)

 

If 2 is added to the second digit of every number, in how many numbers will the second

digit be exactly divisible by the third digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. One.

 

GIVEN

 

• Numbers: 567, 862, 426, 326, 749. Add 2 to each number's second digit; check when (new second digit) is exactly divisible by the (unchanged) third digit.

 

SOLUTION

 

• 567: second digit 6+2=8; third digit 7. Is 8 divisible by 7? No.

 

• 862: second digit 6+2=8; third digit 2. Is 8 divisible by 2? Yes (8÷2=4). ✓

 

• 426: second digit 2+2=4; third digit 6. Is 4 divisible by 6? No.

 

• 326: second digit 2+2=4; third digit 6. Is 4 divisible by 6? No.

 

• 749: second digit 4+2=6; third digit 9. Is 6 divisible by 9? No.

 

• Only 862 satisfies the condition, so the count is One.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Make a quick 3-column table (original 2nd digit, +2 new value, 3rd digit) for all five numbers at once, then scan the 'divisible by' check column-wise — faster and less error-prone than working number-by-number from scratch.

 

NOTE

 

• 'Exactly divisible' means the remainder must be zero — treat divisibility by checking if the third digit divides evenly into the new second digit, not the reverse.

question:
Which of the following letter-clusters will replace the question mark (?) in the given

series to make it logically complete?

 

BBO 2 ECM -4 HDK 8 KEI -16 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. NFG 32.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: BBO 2, ECM −4, HDK 8, KEI −16, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Numbers: 2, −4, 8, −16, ? — each term is the previous term multiplied by −2: 2×(−2)=−4 ✓; −4×(−2)=8 ✓; 8×(−2)=−16 ✓. So the next number = −16×(−2) = 32.

 

• First letters of each cluster: B, E, H, K, ? — B(2), E(5), H(8), K(11): each +3. Next = 11+3=14 = N.

 

• Second letters: B, C, D, E, ? — B(2), C(3), D(4), E(5): each +1. Next = 5+1=6 = F.

 

• Third letters: O, M, K, I, ? — O(15), M(13), K(11), I(9): each −2. Next = 9−2=7 = G.

 

• Combining: next cluster = NFG, with number 32.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a mixed letter+number series into FOUR independent mini-series (three letter-columns + one number-column) and solve each with its own simple step pattern (arithmetic step or constant multiplier) — much easier than trying to track everything at once.

 

NOTE

 

• The number pattern here is a geometric progression (×−2 each time, alternating sign), not arithmetic — always check for multiplication/ratio patterns when a simple addition pattern doesn't fit.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series?

 

214 217 222 229 238 ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. 249.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: 214, 217, 222, 229, 238, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• Differences between consecutive terms: 217−214=3; 222−217=5; 229−222=7; 238−229=9.

 

• The differences form their own series increasing by 2 each time: 3, 5, 7, 9, so the next difference = 11.

 

• Next term = 238 + 11 = 249.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• When consecutive differences themselves increase by a constant amount (here, +2 each time: 3,5,7,9,11...), simply extend that difference-series by one more step and add it to the last given term.

 

NOTE

 

• This is the same 'difference-of-differences is constant' (second-order arithmetic) pattern seen in several other series questions in this paper — always test it early when a simple constant-difference doesn't fit.

question:
What will come in the place of ‘?’ in the following equation, if ‘+’ and ‘-‘ are interchanged

and ‘x’ and ‘÷’ are interchanged?

 

113 ÷ 6 + 98 x 2 - 156 = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option B i.e. 785.

 

GIVEN

 

• Original equation: 113 ÷ 6 + 98 × 2 − 156 = ?, with '+' ↔ '−' interchanged, and '×' ↔ '÷' interchanged.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Replace each symbol with its swapped counterpart: ÷ becomes ×, + becomes −, × becomes ÷, − becomes +.

 

• New equation: 113 × 6 − 98 ÷ 2 + 156 = ?

 

• Apply BODMAS (× and ÷ first): 113 × 6 = 678; 98 ÷ 2 = 49.

 

• Now compute left to right: 678 − 49 + 156 = 629 + 156 = 785.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option B.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• First rewrite the ENTIRE equation with all symbols swapped in one clean pass, then solve it fresh using normal BODMAS — trying to swap-and-calculate simultaneously often causes sign errors.

 

NOTE

 

• Interchanging '+' ↔ '−' and '×' ↔ '÷' is a straightforward substitution, but ALWAYS double check that every occurrence of each symbol was swapped, not just the first one.

question:
In a certain code language,

A + B means ‘A is the sister of B’,

A @ B means ‘A is the brother of B’,

A - B means ‘A is the wife of B’,

and A # B means ‘A is the father of B’.

 

How is O related to V if ‘O @ P + T - G # V’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option C i.e. Mother's brother.

 

GIVEN

 

• Code: '+' = sister of; '@' = brother of; '−' = wife of; '#' = father of. Chain: O @ P + T − G # V.

 

SOLUTION

 

• O @ P: O is the brother of P.

 

• P + T: P is the sister of T. (So P and T are siblings, and O — being P's brother — is also T's brother.)

 

• T − G: T is the wife of G. (So T is female, and married to G.)

 

• G # V: G is the father of V.

 

• Since G is V's father and T is G's wife, T is V's mother.

 

• Since O is T's brother (as derived above), and T is V's mother, O is V's mother's brother, i.e. V's maternal uncle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option C.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• For coded family-tree chains, draw a simple family tree step by step as you decode each symbol (mark gender where the relation reveals it, e.g. 'wife of' ⇒ female) — visualising it avoids losing track over a long chain.

 

NOTE

 

• Track GENDER carefully at each step ('sister', 'wife' reveal female; 'brother', 'father' reveal male) — the final relationship name (e.g. 'mother's brother' vs 'father's brother') depends entirely on correctly gendering each link.

question:
What should come in place of the question mark (?) in the given series based on the

English alphabetical order?

 

VNQ UMP TLO SKN ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option A i.e. RJM.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series: VNQ, UMP, TLO, SKN, ?

 

SOLUTION

 

• First letters: V, U, T, S, ? — V(22), U(21), T(20), S(19): each decreases by 1. Next = 19−1=18 = R.

 

• Second letters: N, M, L, K, ? — N(14), M(13), L(12), K(11): each decreases by 1. Next = 11−1=10 = J.

 

• Third letters: Q, P, O, N, ? — Q(17), P(16), O(15), N(14): each decreases by 1. Next = 14−1=13 = M.

 

• Combining: next cluster = RJM.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option A.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Split a 3-letter cluster series into three separate single-letter columns and find each column's simple step (here, all three columns decrease by exactly 1) — reassembling the answer is then immediate.

 

NOTE

 

• All three letter-columns here happen to follow the SAME step size (−1), which is a good consistency check that your reading of the series is correct.

question:
Mr. Zzz starts from Point A and drives 7 km towards the South. He then takes a left turn,

drives 21 km, turns left and drives 16 km. He then takes a left turn and drives 26 km. He

takes a final left turn, drives 9 km and stops at Point P. How far (shortest distance) and

towards which direction should he drive in order to reach Point A again? (All turns are

90 degrees turns only unless specified).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. 5 km to the East.

 

GIVEN

 

• Path: South 7 km → Left turn, 21 km → Left turn, 16 km → Left turn, 26 km → Left turn, 9 km, stop at P.

 

SOLUTION

 

• Take East = +x, North = +y. Start at A = (0, 0).

 

• South 7 km: (0, −7). Facing south, left turn → East; drive 21 km: (21, −7).

 

• Facing east, left turn → North; drive 16 km: (21, 9).

 

• Facing north, left turn → West; drive 26 km: (−5, 9).

 

• Facing west, left turn → South; drive 9 km: P = (−5, 0).

 

• P is 5 km to the west of A. To return from P to A, Mr. Zzz must travel in the opposite direction: 5 km to the East.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Track only the NET east-west and north-south displacement using a simple running x-y tally as each leg is added — the final return direction and distance are just the reverse of this net (x, y) vector.

 

NOTE

 

• This question follows the identical structure and turn-pattern as Q.55 in this same paper — recognising the repeated question TYPE lets you solve it just as quickly using the same x-y coordinate method.

question:
Refer to the given series and answer the question that follows. All numbers are single

digit numbers only. (Counting to be done from left to right only)

 

(Left) 6 4 9 2 3 2 7 7 9 8 3 8 7 9 9 9 7 9 5 8 9 9 1 (Right)

 

How many such odd digits are there, each of which is immediately preceded by an even

digit and also immediately followed by an odd digit?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option D i.e. Three.

 

GIVEN

 

• Series (23 digits): 6 4 9 2 3 2 7 7 9 8 3 8 7 9 9 9 7 9 5 8 9 9 1

 

SOLUTION

 

• Scan for odd digits with an EVEN digit immediately before AND an ODD digit immediately after.

 

• 1st qualifying spot: '...2 7 7...' (7th digit '7', preceded by even 2, followed by odd 7).

 

• 2nd qualifying spot: '...8 7 9...' (13th digit '7', preceded by even 8, followed by odd 9).

 

• 3rd qualifying spot: '...8 9 9...' (21st digit '9', preceded by even 8, followed by odd 9).

 

• No other odd digit in the series satisfies both conditions simultaneously, giving a total of 3 qualifying digits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option D.

 

SHORT TRICK

 

• Underline every EVEN digit first; then check only the digit immediately AFTER each underlined even digit — if that digit is odd, look one more step ahead to confirm the digit after IT is also odd, to complete the even-odd-odd pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• This condition (even, then odd, then odd) is directionally asymmetric from the 'even-odd-even' pattern seen in Q.53 — read the exact wording of each such question carefully, as the required neighbour pattern often changes.

question:
Approximately how many hectares are targeted for increased forest and tree cover by

2030 as per the Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan released in 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is approximately 24.7 million hectares.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Revised Green India Mission (GIM) Plan, released in 2025, targets an increase in forest and tree cover over an estimated 24.7 million hectares by 2030, in order to meet India's enhanced carbon-sink commitment under its climate goals. (हरित भारत मिशन — 2030 तक लगभग 24.7 मिलियन हेक्टेयर)

 

• This revised, larger figure was calculated to meet India's enhanced Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) target of creating an additional carbon sink of 3.39 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent through forest and tree cover by 2030.

 

• The Green India Mission is one of the eight missions under India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• The original GIM (2014) had a more modest target: to increase forest/tree cover on 5 million hectares and improve the quality of forest cover on another 5 million hectares (10 million hectares total).

 

• GIM is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC) and works through State/UT Forest Departments and local communities.

 

• India's overall NDC under the Paris Agreement commits to creating an additional carbon sink of 2.5 to 3 billion tonnes of CO₂ equivalent through additional forest and tree cover by 2030 — the revised GIM plan is calibrated to help meet this.

 

NOTE

 

• 10 million (Option B) reflects the ORIGINAL (2014) GIM target figure, not the revised 2025 target.

 

• 20 million (Option D): Not the correct figure cited in the revised 2025 GIM plan; the actual estimate is closer to 24.7 million hectares.

question: The Lokpal of India celebrated its 1st Foundation Day on which date in 2025?

question:

question:
Finland became the _____ European country to exit the Ottawa landmine treaty in June

solution_text:

• The Ottawa Treaty (1997), formally the 'Convention on the Prohibition of the Use, Stockpiling, Production and Transfer of Anti-Personnel Mines and on their Destruction', bans the use, production and stockpiling of anti-personnel landmines.

 

• Finland's withdrawal, along with several other Eastern European/Baltic states, was driven by heightened security concerns following Russia's actions in the region, particularly after the Russia-Ukraine conflict.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option A.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other European nations that similarly announced withdrawal from the Ottawa Treaty around this period (2024-2025) include the Baltic states — Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia — and Poland, citing regional security concerns.

 

• The Ottawa Treaty does not include major military powers such as the United States, Russia, China and India among its signatories, limiting its universal effectiveness.

 

• India is not a signatory to the Ottawa (Mine Ban) Treaty, citing its long land borders and security requirements.

 

NOTE

 

• 4th, 3rd and 6th (Options B, C, D): These do not correctly represent Finland's position in the sequence of European countries exiting the treaty; Finland was specifically the 5th.

question:

question:
Which of the following is NOT a main feature of ‘Control of Water Pollution (Grant,

Refusal or Cancellation of Consent) Guidelines', 2025?
solution_text:

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• These guidelines are issued under the framework of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, administered by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs).

 

• 'Consent to Establish (CTE)' and 'Consent to Operate (CTO)' are mandatory clearances industries must obtain from Pollution Control Boards before starting operations that could pollute water bodies.

 

• Streamlining such regulatory consent processes is part of the government's broader 'Ease of Doing Business' push, while still aiming to strengthen environmental safeguards.

 

NOTE

 

• Stricter Location Criteria (Option A), Clear Enforcement of Rules (Option B) and Streamlined Consent Process (Option D): These ARE genuine main features described in the 2025 water pollution consent guidelines, making them incorrect choices for this 'NOT a feature' question.

• iGOT Karmayogi (Integrated Government Online Training) is the online training platform launched under Mission Karmayogi, aimed at capacity-building of civil servants and government employees through structured, role-specific online courses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option C.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mission Karmayogi (National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building - NPCSCB) was launched in 2020 to reform and standardise the training of India's civil servants.

 

• Rozgar Mela recruitment drives cover various central government departments and ministries, with new appointees joining posts in railways, banking, police and other government sectors.

 

• These recruitment and training initiatives together aim to build a skilled, citizen-centric and future-ready government workforce.

 

NOTE

 

• e-Shram Portal (Option A): A database/registration platform for unorganised sector workers, not a training platform for new government recruits.

 

• National Career Service (Option B): An online portal connecting job seekers with employment opportunities and career counselling, not specifically the training platform used for Rozgar Mela recruits.

 

• SWAYAM (Option D): An online education platform mainly for academic/higher-education courses, not the specific platform used for training new Rozgar Mela government recruits.
